sections.text: Introduction

The REL 531 digital line protection scheme is designed for the high - speed 
discriminative protection of lines and cables in distribution and transmission 
systems. The rated voltage of the line being protected is not a restriction and 
the protection is applicable to solidly or low-resistance grounded systems, 
systems with Petersen coils or to ungrounded systems.

All kinds of faults are detected including close-in three-phase, cross-country 
faults, evolving faults and high-resistance earth faults

This procedure details the steps required to completely check the proper 
operation and calibration of the relay. It is recommended this procedure be 
carried out on an annually bases. The document is formatted the way to minimize 
the possibility of error causing personal injury 
or damage to equipment.

The first draft initiated by eng. Ehab Zakaria, tested by eng. Sidhom Nassef, 
revised by eng. Adel El-Nagar: MDEPC quality control engineer, accepted by eng. Aly Zahran: 
general manager & eng. Samir Abdel-Gilil: MDEPC quality control general director, approved by eng. Ahmad Sawan: head sector of Nubaria 
PS, and certified by eng. Mohamed Naguib:
MDEPC
quality 
control head sector.

Safety 
Precautions
A work permit must be issued.
The maintenance staff should be trained, qualified, and carry the suitable ID safety category.
Safety fence with caution marks surrounding the work area is required.

Wear the appropriate 
 safety and healthy equipment as safety 
 shoes, safety helmet ... etc
Line isolation is required.

Make sure that CT secondary circuits are shorted before isolating the 
 current circuits for test distance protection.
Transmission Line must be grounded.

Preparation

Make sure CT secondary circuits are shorted at the incoming terminal blocks 
 before isolate the relay current circuits for test.

Be sure that the DC power of the relay is correct by applying a DC voltmeter 
 across points X18 (17,18 see fig.1) on the rear of the relay.

Note: Don't forget to GENERATE PREFAULT CONDITION [I=0.001A, 
V=57V].

From TEST SELECTION choose automatic time zone (Z/T) and dont forget to 
adjust the test sequence as follow [fault =all faults, Z min=zero, Z max =as the 
setting, STEP =0.5 OHM, Angle [degree]=0, after that click OK the tester will 
operate and test the R axis.
Repeat 1- BUT chose angle=90 the tester will test the X axis.
Choose STORE ALL TESTS >>>>

Go to RESULTS from main menu chose HEADER and apply all information about these 
feeder and ok
Now print the results and you have complete test results for these relay.

From TEST SELECTION choose Click and test and by curser click on the point which 
you need to test [generally choose all points on X and Y Axis].
Repeat steps from 3 to 5.
Now you have complete test results for these relay.

sections.text:
Switch on to Fault ( 
SOTF )

From main menu select test selection select SOTF test and plot the 
setting from Rio file.
Make prefault at zero current and voltage.
Click ok.
Inject current and voltage as fault case in any zone Z2 or Z3
Click Start.
Choose STORE ALL TESTS.
From results will see that the time at all faults is equal to Z1 time.

sections.text:
Auto Recloser 
Test

From main menu select TEST SELECTION select AUTO RECLOSER test and plot the 
setting from Rio file.
CB should be closed and disconnecting switches are opened.
Set the auto recloser parameter, and then press OK.

Make trip at any zone by inject fault current and voltage ( CB will be tripped 
 and then A/R reclose it ).
Choose store all tests.

sections.text: Earth Fault (E/F)

RUN ISA WIZARD software and choose GENERATION AND DISTRIBUTION RELAYS>>>> X-PRO 
>>>>MANUAL MODE>>>>
GENERATE PREFAULT CONDITION [I=0.001A].
Disable distance function.

SELECT FAULT AND INJECT CURRENT VALUE EQUAL TO (I Setting*1.01) to determine the 
operating time.
Click Start.
Repeat steps from 1 to 5 for all phases R, S, and T.

note that: the injection should be on phase by phase not on three phases 
or on two phases.
Chose store all tests.

sections.text:
Return Relay and Associated 
Equipment to Service
Enable any function which was disabled

Return relay to service by removing the test leads from the relay terminals and 
the test set.
Make sure CT and VT secondary circuits are in normal condition.
Remove the disturbance alarm LED's on the relay which is caused by the test.
Request feeder to be returned in service.

Take pharos readings of all AC currents and voltages and compare them to those 
for normal load condition.

Check that these reading agree with station meters (MW, 
Mvar, Amperes and power 
factor).
Place a copy of the test result in the field maintenance file.
